title: `intent daemon start` with a pipe on stdin can start a daemon that stops at once, and its refusal's remedy does not name the lifeline
body:
Found on 2026-11-12 while re-driving docs/known-defects.md on gyges for the 3.3.1 cut (hv decision 43), on the pair at 594422fb48c0.

`intent daemon start` hands its own stdin to intentd when that stdin is a pipe (`stdin_is_a_lifeline`, ST0073), and intentd then takes the pipe's writer as its owner and stops when the pipe reaches end of file. Over ssh without a terminal, a command's stdin is a pipe: `stat -L -f %HT /dev/stdin` reads `Fifo File` on gyges, where a Claude Code shell on rhadamanth reads `Character Device`. In the known-defects drive run that way, intentd logged `intentd stopping: the lifeline closed, so whoever started this daemon is gone` at the same millisecond as its `listening` line, and `daemon start` refused with exit 1:

    error: intentd was started and is not answering
      remedy: it either failed to bind or exited. Its output is in `<state>/intentd.log` and `<state>/intentd.err.log`, which is where the reason will be.

The remedy names neither stdin nor the lifeline. intentd.err.log is empty, and only intentd.log says why. The same drive with stdin from /dev/null starts a daemon that answers, and the drive's 0443 entry then reproduces as it did at 3.3.0.

Not fully explained: in one probe of the same ssh shape, an unpiped `intent daemon start` started a daemon that stayed up, so when the pipe's writer goes away depends on the session. The failing shape is pinned by refs/bank/ic/kd331/daemon-probe3.sh, which runs `intent daemon start 2>&1 | sed 's/^/  /'` in a scratch project under a short isolated HOME, as the drive's `run` does, and by the drive's first log, refs/bank/ic/kd331/drive-kd331-594422fb48c0-run1-pipedstdin.log, whose 0443 entry searched in-process for this reason.

The fix, on vc's ruling of 2026-11-12: cc fixes the remedy, so that a daemon stopped by its lifeline is reported as that, after issue 0689, since the remedy's meaning is the core's. It rides 3.3.1 under directive 1.


## Resolution

Fixed for 3.3.1 at b13fcd526, banked as `refs/bank/cc/0690/whole-proved-on-e05e2d604` and landed by vc. When this command's stdin was a pipe, the remedy of "intentd was started and is not answering" now names the lifeline: intentd took the pipe as its lifeline and stops when it reaches end of file, as it can at once over ssh without a terminal; `<state>/intentd.log` says the lifeline closed when that is why; and `intent daemon start </dev/null` starts a daemon that stays up. Otherwise it failed to bind or exited, and its output is in intentd.log and intentd.err.log. Without a pipe the remedy is unchanged. On ic's read, the text a user reads cites no thread id, since one names a thread of the user's own project or none (issue 0574), and the doc comment keeps ST0073; that wording is banked as `refs/bank/cc/0690b/whole-proved-on-92a79d3cc`, which cc proved on gyges at 92a79d3cc with the render tests passing 25 of 25 and check format and clippy clean. The text is the CLI's own, so ALL_VARIANTS does not move and cut-surface.md is not regenerated. The fix takes a CHANGELOG entry under Fixed in [3.3.1].

Proved by cc on gyges on 2026-11-12, in a worktree of the clone of rhadamanth's main at e05e2d604, with the stamps as cc read them. The arm alone, on the code as it was, did not compile: two E0425 errors on `started_and_not_answering`, the seam the fix adds (10:55:09Z to 10:55:42Z). With the fix, `bin/devbin test rust --exclude intentsvcs --exclude intentd --exclude testkit --lib render::tests` passed 25 of 25, `a_daemon_that_does_not_answer_is_told_of_the_lifeline_only_when_stdin_was_one` among them, and `bin/devbin check clippy`, `check panics`, `check ownership` and `check format` each exited 0 (10:57:51Z to 10:58:10Z). A first green failed `check format` on one call's layout; the fix half took rustfmt's layout, and the whole green ran again on it. The logs are at `refs/bank/cc/0690/evidence/`. When the pipe's writer goes away over ssh is not pinned here.
